axis: bare possibility, merely not ruled out → endorsed as practically sound

members.tone: The bare floor of the family - it says only that the thing is not ruled out, and promises nothing about anyone being able to bring it off.
Formal and effortful, it frames the thing as a task with a finish line where *possible* frames nothing at all.
Warmer than *accomplishable* - it treats the thing as a goal worth reaching and quietly credits whoever would reach it.
The plainest and most informal of the set, it shrinks a thing down to size in a way *accomplishable* never manages.
Concedes that the thing will take effort and says it fits inside capacity anyway, a fainter endorsement than *achievable*.
Formal, and it looks past the doing to the outcome - the thing brought from prospect into fact.
Technical and colourless: it rates whether a claim can be stood behind, and passes no judgement on the claim itself.
Blunter in its verb than *affirmable* - putting a claim forward rather than standing behind one - but it carries no more approval.
Points at something wanted and says the reach is long enough, giving it a pull toward the goal that *possible* has none of.
Informal and homely, it makes the thing sound simply within arm's length, deflating the reach that *attainable* dignifies.
The one member that withholds - it grants the possibility and in the same breath refuses to promise it, hedging where *feasible* endorses.
A working verdict rather than a hope: it says the thing can be done with what is at hand now, a test *possible* never applies.
The most procedural of the set, it asks only whether the steps can be carried out and offers no opinion on whether they should be.
Formal and faintly grudging, it certifies that a thing can be put into practice without claiming it will go well, unlike *viable*.
The strongest endorsement here - it declares a plan sound enough to go ahead on as things stand, where *workable* says only that it will function.
Modest and practical - it promises the thing will function, not that it will succeed.
